items.rationale: Glazing is excluded under 2.6.4 and 3.5; the optional glazing peril is not shown as agreed (as in Case 3), so t=0.
Drilling is glazing work under 1.3 and an ancillary charge, and the glazing peril is not agreed, so it is not covered.

items.description: Installation of new glass into frame
items.rationale: Fitting the glazing element is glazing work under 3.5(b), and the peril is not agreed, so t=0.
Removing the remains of an item whose damage is not covered follows that item (5.2.1, 7.1.11), so t=0.

items.description: Repair of dented solid-wood side table
items.rationale: Sudden accidental damage to freestanding furniture is covered under 2.6 and contents cover, and the solid-wood table is not a glazing element. The price follows the Case 3 timber repair level, about 300 EUR.

items.description: Touch-up of pre-existing scratches on second cabinet
items.rationale: Pre-existing condition on an unaffected item is excluded under 3.6 and 7.1.9, so t=0.
One attendance by the building services undertaking is payable because covered table repair was done at that visit (7.1.12). References show these charges are small.
A return visit is not separately indemnified under 7.1.12 without prior insurer agreement, so t=0.
Administrative charges on top of itemised labour are not repair costs under 7.1.8(b), so t=0.
